A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MORALLENS study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM evaluations on 640 trolley vignettes, model comparisons, rationale analyses and human validation of the judge.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds preference-dataset comparisons, prompt and judge robustness tests, and model-family analyses.

M1.justification: The 16-rationale taxonomy, reasoning elicitation and LLM-judge classification procedure remain unchanged. Inverse-rank rationale weighting was already documented in v1 Appendix C.3.1; its appearance in v2's main-text equation does not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 640 English trolley vignettes, demographic dimensions, group-size conditions and reasoning-order tasks. New checkpoint and judge comparisons reuse this coverage, and the added paraphrases explicitly preserve the moral scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 4 retains all four original SFT/DPO pairs and adds Tülu 2 13B SFT plus twelve Tülu 2.5 DPO variants. Appendix C.3.4 also evaluates GPT-4o and GPT-4.1 mini as alternative judges alongside Gemini 2.5 Flash, substantially expanding the comparison set.

E3.justification: v2 adds a shared-SFT-base control across twelve preference-tuned variants and nine-model evaluations varying prompt paraphrases and judge identity. Section 4.3 also replaces UTILITY's saved-lives-ratio wording with an equally weighted frequency over 320 imbalanced vignettes. This revises the reported metric specification without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's weighting and choice-order analyses, v2 tests sensitivity to preference-training data, three prompt paraphrases and alternative judges. It also adds within-family versus cross-family scaling analysis and quantifies selection of the 'Other' category.

E5.justification: New analyses report Spearman correlations, variance-explained significance tests, a binomial test across model families, and dispersion of 'Other' selection. The existing five-sample/three-sample scheme and 95% confidence-interval reporting remain unchanged; no increase in repeated runs is stated.

E6.justification: New Table 4 entries give Tülu DPO CDGAP values of 0.12–0.41 against the shared SFT value of 0.17. Tables 9–10 add robustness results, including average CDGAP Pearson correlations of 0.934 across paraphrases and 0.989 across judges. Appendix D.1 reports negative size correlations in 13 of 16 families. Original comparison rows retain their values.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 revises the mathematical metric specifications: UTILITY becomes an indicator mean, and CDGAP receives an explicit weighted double sum. The latter lacks normalization needed for its claimed [-1,1] range and is not equivalent as written to v1's difference of proportions. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: the rationale taxonomy, contrasting pre-decision and post-decision reasoning, and capability-dependent differences between balanced and imbalanced dilemmas.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 replaces the emphasis on larger models becoming more deontological after DPO with a dataset-dependent interpretation lacking an inherent directional effect. Consistently increasing UTILITY becomes increasing or stable in nearly all cases. New discussion interprets robustness and within-family scaling, and further qualifies the taxonomy and trolley-task applicability.

D1.justification: Table 8 adds checkpoint identifiers and temperatures for the Tülu variants. v2 newly documents human-annotator blinding, corrects the Qwen thinking-mode command, and revises estimated API expenditure from 300 to 800 USD. The code-access information and hardware description remain.

R1.justification: The Lambert et al. (2024) Tülu 3 citation and bibliography entry are removed, although Tülu 3 results remain in Table 4. Appendix A and the broader positioning against prior moral-judgment research are unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes comprise a localized rewrite of Section 5.4, expanded metric and taxonomy explanations, additional appendix subsections, and wording, cross-reference and affiliation edits. The overall narrative and main section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 4 expands to a full-width display, Table 8 gains rows, and new Tables 9, 10 and 12 present robustness and family-grouped results. Existing figures retain their graphical content but are relocated, with limited caption terminology changes and appendix layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: The shared-base DPO comparison and added prompt/judge checks strengthen empirical support and produce a better-qualified alignment interpretation. These gains are tempered by the new CDGAP equation's missing normalization and internally inconsistent wording in the paraphrase protocol, which impair clarity and reproducibility.
